title: Robust perturbation-based regression harness for INT8 weight-only quant profiles (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Objective: Build an integration and regression harness that validates INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ/AWQ variants) against a robust set of perturbation tests and semantic-accuracy checks, to be used in CI, nightly regression runs, and canary rollouts.

Problem statement: Current profile validation primarily focuses on golden-answer equality and end-to-end smoke tests. This yields false negatives and misses subtle semantic regressions (e.g., paraphrase sensitivity, distributional logprob shifts, and hallucination rate increases) that only surface in production under diverse prompts and sequence lengths. We need a reproducible, low-flakiness harness that: (1) exercises calibration artifacts (shadow/calibration-snapshots), (2) measures semantic drift using embeddings and logprob statistics, (3) stresses per-layer quantization edge cases across GPT-family checkpoints, and (4) integrates telemetry flags for automated rollback when thresholds are exceeded.

Scope: Implement a perturbation-driven suite that mutates prompts (lexical paraphrases, punctuation/noise injection, length truncation/extension), runs profiles for GPTQ and AWQ variants, and computes multi-dimensional deltas: embedding cosine similarity, answer token-level logprob delta, top-k token distribution KL, and task-specific metrics (ROUGE for summarization slices, semantic-answer match for Q/A). The harness will run on the nightly matrix: models = {gpt-3-family-lite, gpt-3.5-legacy, gpt-4-compat-open}, seqlen = {128, 512, 2048}, hardware tags = {ampere-A100, h100-80g, t4}, and batch sizes = {1, 4}.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to promote profile):
- No semantic similarity regression: mean embedding cosine delta <= 0.02 on golden prompt set and <= 0.05 on perturbed set.
- Logprob shift: median per-token logprob delta <= 0.15 nats between FP16 baseline and INT8 profile for the same prompts.
- Top-k KL divergence: average KL(top-50) <= 0.08.
- Task-specific thresholds: ROUGE-L drop <= 1.5 points for summarization shards; answer-span F1 drop <= 2.0 for Q/A shards.
- Canary pass: a 72h canary with traffic ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with no error-rate increase > 0.3% and no SLO regressions.

Calibration workflow integration: Harness will consume calibration snapshots (calibration-ledger IDs) and replay calibration seed states. We'll add a binary-search step to locate layer-wise scale/clipping anomalies for failing profiles and emit a per-profile "calibration fingerprint" to the profile registry for rollback mapping.

CI & orchestration: Add a new job quant/perturbation-regress that runs fast smoke subset on PRs (5 models x 2 seqlen x 10 perturb seeds) and a full job for nightly/regression orchestration. Integrate results with the telemetry aggregator (https://dashboards.internal.redwood/quant/perturbation) and add auto-ticketing for regressions exceeding alert thresholds.

Rollout and fallback: Add a runtime policy that will route a configurable fraction of requests to the INT8 profile and fallback to FP16 baseline automatically if the profile returns inconsistent top-1 responses greater than 0.5% within a sliding 10-minute window. Document operational rollback steps and automations in the runbook.

Artifacts: Confluence spec (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/QP/perturbation-harness-v1), PR template (https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/xxxx), and reference dataset (s3://redwood-quant/perturbation-datasets/v1).
tasks: Design perturbation taxonomy and seed generator (lexical, punctuation, paraphrase, length)
Implement CI job quant/perturbation-regress with fast-PR and nightly modes
Integrate embedding-based similarity check and logprob delta computations into harness
Wire up calibration-ledger replay and binary-search diagnostic flow
Add telemetry markers and dashboard panels for per-profile drift
Define canary ramp policy and failure thresholds; implement automatic fallback
Write regression-to-PR auto-ticketing and flakiness suppression heuristics
Author runbook and SRE actionable checklist for profile rollback
